name: Changelog

sources.title: Submit News — free submission requires sign-in; URL + title + 'what's interesting' (markdown); explicit rejections: how-tos/tutorials, commercial products/services ('Sponsorship is your path'), reader-hostile sites; submitters emailed if published
Sponsorship pricing — the catalog's stored URL; Changelog $3,000/wk (2 episodes, 4wk min), Changelog News $1,500/wk, Practical AI $1,200/ep, Fallthrough $200/ep; adam@changelog.com

requirements: Free Changelog account (sign in/up) — the submission form needs a profile for attribution/notification
Submit News takes: URL, title, and 'What's interesting about it?' (markdown)
Explicitly rejected: how-to/tutorials, commercial products/services (use Sponsorship), reader-hostile websites, podcast suggestions (use /request)
Developer-news audience — 'if your fellow devs will find it interesting, submit it'; submitting your own work is allowed and encouraged
Paid sponsorship is separate and substantial ($200–$3,000/wk depending on show)
preparation: A genuinely interesting dev-facing link — OSS release, technical writeup, dev tool of substance
A compelling 'what's interesting' pitch — they get a lot of submissions
workflow: If published you're notified by email — no response means not picked
For commercial promotion use the Sponsorship page instead (adam@changelog.com)
watchFor: Commercial product promotion in Submit News is explicitly rejected — pure product pitches will be declined; open-source/dev-interest angles only
The catalog's stored URL was the sponsor-pricing page — the free editorial route is /news/submit
High volume — no notification unless published
The Changelog network also runs podcasts; 'Request Episode' is a different form at /request
countsAsLive: The submission is published on Changelog News (changelog.com/news) and you're emailed
unknowns: Editorial review time for news submissions
Whether Changelog++ membership affects submission consideration
